 Boston Red Sox pitcher Johan Oviedo (29) delivers in the first inning of a spring training baseball game against the Minnesota Twins in Fort Myers, Fla., Wednesday, Feb. 25, 2026. (AP Photo/Gerald Herbert) 
 By Gabrielle Starr | gstarr@bostonherald.com PUBLISHED: November 20, 2026 at 6:19 PM EST Getting your Trinity Audio player ready... Shortly after tendering one-year contracts to all 12 eligible players before Friday’s 5 p.m. ET non-tender deadline, the Boston Red Sox traded one of the pitchers on the list who missed nearly the entire 2026 season due to injuries.
 Boston dealt right-hander Johan Oviedo to the Arizona Diamondbacks, as first reported by FanSided’s Robert Murray. The Red Sox will receive minor-league left-hander Luke Dotson and a player to be named later.
 Oviedo pitched in the March 30 game of Boston’s opening road trip before going on the injured list for the remainder of the season. The Red Sox acquired him and left-hander Tyler Samaniego from the Pittsburgh Pirates last fall.
 The Diamondbacks selected Dotson in the 11th round of the 2025 MLB Draft, out of Mississippi State University. He made his professional debut this year, splitting the season between Low-A and High-A, posting a combined 3.00 ERA over 34 relief appearances, with 64 strikeouts and 16 walks in 45 innings.
 The list of tendered Red Sox players include several others who missed most or all of at least the past season due to injury, including right-handers Tanner Houck and Kutter Crawford, and first baseman Triston Casas. The Red Sox have actively explored trade interest in Houck and Crawford as well, though their current projected starting rotation is lefty-heavy with Garrett Crochet, Ranger Suarez, Payton Tolle and Jake Bennett.
 Houck missed most of the 2025 and 2026 seasons due to Tommy John surgery before making his return to the mound on the last day of the regular season. Crawford last pitched on a big-league mound in 2024; knee and arm injuries have repeatedly sidelined him since. Casas required season-ending knee surgery early in May 2025, and due to several setbacks has not played in a professional game since; he also missed most of the ’24 season due to a rib cartilage injury.
 Jarren Duran will also be tendered a contract, though the Red Sox are actively trying to trade him. They have explored trading Duran throughout the last three offseasons.
 The Red Sox did not, however, reach agreement with any of the tendered players on salary.
